questions.q: What are Sentinel's built-in workbook templates actually tied to?
options: A specific data connector — the template only has data once that source is connected
The analyst's individual Azure AD account
A specific Sentinel pricing tier
Nothing; they work identically regardless of what's connected
questions.explain: Each built-in template, like the Azure AD Sign-in Logs workbook, is built for one data source and stays empty until the matching connector is enabled and sending data.

questions.q: What does the Azure AD Sign-in Logs workbook template visualize, once the right connector is enabled?
options: Authentication activity, such as successful/failed sign-ins over time and risky sign-in trends
Firewall rule changes on network devices
Source code commits from a connected repository
Email attachment scanning results only
questions.explain: The Azure AD Sign-in Logs workbook surfaces sign-in activity: successful and failed attempts over time, sign-ins by location, and risky sign-in trends.

questions.q: How much effort does activating a built-in workbook template typically take?
options: Close to one click — find the matching template and save it, already wired to the right data
A multi-week KQL development project
It requires rewriting the entire data connector first
It can only be done by Microsoft support directly
questions.explain: Activating a built-in template is close to a one-click action: find the template matching an enabled connector and click Save.

questions.q: Why would a built-in workbook NOT be enough for a request like "a workbook combining failed logins with our specific VIP account list"?
options: Because Microsoft has no way to know an individual organization's VIP accounts, so no template ships with that built in
Because built-in workbooks can't display KQL query results at all
Because VIP accounts can never appear in sign-in logs
Because custom workbooks are disabled in Sentinel by default
questions.explain: Built-in templates solve common, well-understood scenarios; anything specific to one organization's own priorities, like a VIP list, requires a custom workbook.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's an alternative to starting a custom workbook from a completely blank canvas?
options: Cloning a built-in template and editing it as a starting point
Disabling all data connectors first
Exporting the data to Excel and building the chart there instead
Waiting for Microsoft to release a matching template
questions.explain: Sentinel allows cloning a built-in template and editing it, which is often faster than starting a custom workbook from scratch.
